create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

oidc_jwt.description: The UserInfo endpoint returns claims depending on the granted scopes rather than a fixed schema.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID/OAuth claims and userinfo endpoint docs
oidc_jwt.note: Missing email/profile/metadata claims after login may simply mean the corresponding scopes were not granted, not that identity data was stripped or misbound.

oidc_jwt.description: The UserInfo endpoint only accepts an access token of a user, not a client or pure machine token.
oidc_jwt.note: Machine-to-machine JWT profile grants may fail or return unsuitable identity data at UserInfo without indicating a security issue.

oidc_jwt.description: Certain reserved scopes intentionally alter audience or enforce organization membership/domain constraints.
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization differences caused by reserved scopes are expected and must be isolated from security findings.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo returns only claims allowed by the granted scopes; sub is always present but profile/email/roles/metadata claims appear only when requested or configured.
oidc_jwt.note: Avoid flagging missing optional claims as identity loss or authorization bugs when the corresponding scopes were not requested.

oidc_jwt.description: Token introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-client introspection failures are expected by design and should not be mistaken for token revocation or parsing errors.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh-token requests may only ask for a scope subset of the original authorization; omitted scope reuses the original scope.
oidc_jwt.note: A narrowed or rejected refresh response is expected behavior, not evidence of inconsistent authorization.

oidc_jwt.description: If requested_token_type is omitted in token exchange, ZITADEL defaults to an access token.
oidc_jwt.note: Receiving an access token without explicitly requesting one is by design and should not be flagged as type confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Requesting reserved project audience scopes adds project IDs to the access-token audience by design.
oidc_jwt.note: Additional audience values caused by reserved scopes are intentional and should not be treated as audience overgrant.

oidc_jwt.description: Token introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-client introspection failures should not be mistaken for revoked or invalid tokens.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange only allows audience values that are a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejection for out-of-set audiences is compliant behavior and should not be flagged as a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange returns an id_token only when openid scope is requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat missing id_token as a bug when openid was not requested.

oidc_jwt.description: The subject returned by ZITADEL tokens and UserInfo is ZITADEL's internal subject ID, not necessarily the original upstream JWT assertion sub string used in machine JWT bearer grant setup.
oidc_jwt.note: Direct string comparison between sent JWT sub and granted /userinfo sub will create false I4 positives for machine/service-account JWT flows.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, iss equal to sub, exp in the future for control cases, and iat not older than 1 hour. Use control claims like iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Without a valid control assertion, LOGIN_FAILED may reflect malformed JWT-profile grant construction rather than freshness enforcement.

For I1 proof-integrity tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT header MUST include kid matching the downloaded keyId. ZITADEL documentation states key identification requires a kid header; missing or wrong kid can fail before signature-trust logic is exercised, confounding resign_attacker_key and kid_injection results.

For I1 issuer/audience validation tests on login_with_jwt, the assertion aud MUST include https://{issuer-domain} and iss/sub normally equal the service-account or application identifier from the downloaded key JSON. If aud is omitted or wrong, failures are expected by design and do not isolate signature-validation behavior.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti on login_with_jwt, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT bearer assertion as a vulnerability unless the docs explicitly promise one-time assertion tracking. The provided ZITADEL docs describe JWT profile grant validation requirements but do not document jti replay prevention.

For token_exchange audience-binding tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is by design and should not be interpreted as a token-exchange bug.

For token_exchange token-type tests, respect ZITADEL's supported token-type matrix: subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:refresh_token is not allowed; subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt is only allowed in combination with actor_token; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. Invalid combinations will fail by design and must not be used as security oracles.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's granted scope and claims against the original authorization. ZITADEL documents that invalid_scope is returned when requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner, so the fuzzer MUST request an expanded scope intentionally and assert rejection or non-escalation rather than assuming silent narrowing.

For I1/I5 cross-client token introspection tests, introspect_token only returns active=true when the requesting client is part of the token audience. A false/limited introspection result from a non-audience client is by design and must not be treated as token invalidity or audience confusion in the token itself.

For verify_granted_identity, send the access_token as Bearer token, not the id_token. ZITADEL explicitly documents that /oidc/v1/userinfo requires the access token of the user; using id_token will produce misleading failures unrelated to identity binding.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, redirect_uri matching is exact at both authorize and token steps. A mismatch is expected to yield invalid_grant/authorization failure by design, so redirect_uri_mismatch should be tested as flow rejection via status/error handling, not as an identity oracle.

For OIDC nonce-related tests, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. A valid control for code-flow tests SHOULD include nonce in start_oidc_auth so that id_token replay/binding behavior can be assessed consistently; for implicit-flow tests, omitting nonce is malformed by design.

For OIDC state-swap and flow-coherence tests, preserve all original query parameters across redirects and callbacks. The JWT IdP documentation explicitly warns that proxied requests to ZITADEL must forward all original query parameters intact because they preserve critical OIDC flow state; losing them invalidates the test setup rather than exposing a broker flaw.

For OIDC external JWT IdP scenarios, the upstream JWT must be delivered in an HTTP header, never as a URL parameter. The docs explicitly prescribe header transport and note that ZITADEL validates signature, issuer, and expiry only after extracting the JWT from the configured header. Tests using query-parameter token injection are invalid for this platform.

For OIDC external JWT IdP issuer-validation tests, configure the upstream JWT so iss matches the configured JWT IdP issuer and use a control token with valid signature and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Otherwise, rejection may simply reflect documented issuer/expiry enforcement rather than the targeted attack pattern.

For OIDC external JWT IdP freshness tests, ZITADEL documentation explicitly states the JWT must not be expired. Use attack tokens with exp={{now_epoch_minus_3600}} and control tokens with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Without a control, failures cannot be distinguished from broken IdP/header configuration.

For OIDC external JWT IdP trust-anchor tests, ZITADEL validates the JWT signature using keys from the configured Keys Endpoint. To test trust_anchor_substitution correctly, keep the configured Keys Endpoint fixed to the legitimate issuer and vary only the presented token/issuer; otherwise, reconfiguring the trust source changes the test semantics.

For PKCE tests on exchange_code_for_token, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Any other method or missing verifier when PKCE was used at authorize time is malformed by design and should be asserted as flow rejection, not identity mismatch.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include exp and iat claims, and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} for control tokens; use exp={{now_epoch_minus_N}} for expired-token attacks. Tokens with stale iat may fail for setup reasons unrelated to exp/nbf enforcement.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN}). A wrong or missing aud causes rejection before issuer-related checks are reached, so control and attack tokens must keep aud valid while varying only the targeted field.

For I1 kid-related tests on login_with_jwt and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT header kid is required to identify the registered key. Omitting kid can fail as key lookup/setup error rather than proving secure rejection of attacker-controlled keys. Keep kid valid for control tests and vary only the trust target under test.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti against login_with_jwt, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT bearer assertion as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation describes stateless JWT bearer grant usage and does not document jti replay tracking; replay resistance is not guaranteed here.

For token_exchange audience-binding tests, audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that set, rejection is by design; valid control cases must first ensure the requested audience is within the documented subset rule.

For token_exchange scope-escalation tests, invalid_scope can be returned when requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. A valid I5 test must compare an exchange requesting a subset/control scope versus an expanded scope, and interpret invalid_scope as compliant behavior rather than a harness failure.

For token_exchange token-type tests, respect ZITADEL's supported token type matrix: refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token, actor_token, or requested_token_type; JWT subject_token is only allowed in combination with actor_token; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. Using unsupported combinations causes by-design rejection and must not be flagged as security behavior.

For OIDC flow coherence tests using start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token, redirect_uri must match exactly between authorization request and token request. Any mismatch yields invalid_grant by design, so I3 tests must keep redirect_uri constant unless specifically testing redirect_uri_mismatch.

For PKCE-based exchange_code_for_token tests, code_challenge_method must be S256; this is the only supported algorithm. Non-S256 values are setup-invalid and should not be used to infer security properties beyond documented unsupported configuration.

For OIDC nonce-related testing, nonce is REQUIRED for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. Missing nonce in implicit-flow tests can cause by-design failure; nonce mismatch/replay tests must include a control request with a valid nonce and keep all other parameters unchanged.

For verify_granted_identity, UserInfo requires an access_token of a user, not a client. Tokens obtained via client_credentials or machine JWT profile may not yield user claims at /oidc/v1/userinfo; use introspect_token for machine/service-account verification instead of treating UserInfo failure as an identity-binding bug.

For introspect_token, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience. Cross-client introspection failures are by design; use the same audience-bound client for control and attack cases when testing token validity rather than audience membership.

For revoke_session and introspect_token, client authentication is required by the endpoint family documentation ('depending on your authorization method you will have to provide additional parameters or headers'). Tests must authenticate the client consistently using either client_secret_basic/body credentials or private_key_jwt; unauthenticated failures are setup errors, not security outcomes.

For reserved-scope authorization tests, scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}, urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname}, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud have documented side effects on membership enforcement and token audience. Keep these scopes out of generic controls unless the test explicitly targets those behaviors, or they will change authorization outcomes by design.

For I5 metadata-claim tests, the reserved claim urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata returns base64-encoded values when requested. Oracles must decode or compare encoded forms appropriately; apparent type/value mismatches in raw token/userinfo output may be by design encoding rather than authorization escalation.

For I1 proof-integrity tests on login_with_jwt, the assertion aud claim MUST include the ZITADEL issuing domain exactly as documented (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} in examples). If aud is wrong or omitted, failures are expected and do not prove signature/key validation behavior.

For I1 proof-integrity tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT header kid MUST identify the downloaded keyId. ZITADEL documentation states it is necessary to provide a JWT with a kid header claim representing the keyId. Missing or wrong kid can cause rejection before the platform reaches the intended signature-trust test.

For JWT bearer grant assertions and private_key_jwt client authentication, ZITADEL requires iat within the last hour; this is not a configurable leeway sentinel. Never reuse stale assertions across long test runs. Generate fresh iat={{now_epoch}} for each request.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is by design and not evidence of a bug in downstream authorization binding.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, requested scope on refresh_token and token_exchange MUST be treated as constrained by prior authorization. ZITADEL documents refresh_token scope must be a subset of the originally requested scope, and token endpoint may return invalid_scope when requested scope exceeds granted scope. Use a baseline token with narrow scope, then request broader scope during exchange and assert rejection or unchanged claims.

For I5 token_exchange tests, subject_token_type and requested_token_type must use only documented token type identifiers. In particular, refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token or requested_token_type in ZITADEL's token exchange matrix. Using unsupported token types yields by-design failure and must not be reported as an authorization-binding issue.

For I5 token_exchange tests involving openid, remember that id_token is only returned when openid scope is requested. Absence of id_token without openid is by design and must not be interpreted as claim stripping or inconsistent identity behavior.

For I4 identity verification, verify_granted_identity returns sub as ZITADEL's internal subject identifier, not the original JWT bearer assertion sub string for service-account JWT grants. Do not compare the sent JWT sub directly to /userinfo sub for login_with_jwt machine flows; use this endpoint only to confirm granted claims/scopes, not upstream-sub preservation.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, redirect_uri must match exactly between start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token, and must exactly match a preregistered redirect URI. Any mismatch causes invalid_grant/authorization failure by design and is required flow binding, not an I3 bug.

For OIDC implicit-flow or request sequences using response_type containing id_token, nonce MUST be provided. ZITADEL documents nonce as MUST for implicit flow and uses it to mitigate replay. Missing nonce failures are by design and should not be treated as unrelated login instability.

For OIDC RP-style tests using start_oidc_auth, state is only recommended, not mandatory. Do not infer a vulnerability solely because the platform accepts requests without state; state is a client-side CSRF defense parameter, and absence of state in a request is not proof of server-side flow incoherence.

For OIDC RP-style tests using prompt=none, id_token_hint SHOULD be provided per documentation. If prompt=none without a usable existing session or hint returns interaction_required/login_required, that is by design and not a replay or session-binding flaw.

For verify_granted_identity and introspect_token comparisons, claims are scope-dependent. UserInfo and introspection only return additional user claims when corresponding scopes were granted. Missing email/profile/roles/metadata claims without requested scopes is by design and must not be flagged as identity confusion or privilege loss.

For I5 audience tests against issued access tokens, note that ZITADEL's reserved scopes can intentionally add project IDs to the access-token audience (for example urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud). If such scopes are requested, extra audience values are expected and must not be treated as audience overgrant.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
